title: Ops field notes: latency-cost correlations (week of 2026-03-30)
content:
Quick summary:
- This week we focused on two cross-cutting issues: a subtle latency uplift for small-chat requests and a correlated rise in inference cost for a subset of customers using 8-bit quantized variants. We believe both are tied to changes in batching and KV-cache hit patterns introduced by the autoscaler change on 2026-03-24.

Standup notes (chronological):
2026-03-30 (Mon)
- Observed: P50 latency for short-chat path rose ~18% between 03:00–05:00 UTC. Not global, concentrated in us-west-2 serving nodes.
- Trace sample: high proportion of rehydrated KV-cache misses causing extra ATTACH spans; additional span time ~15–40ms on avg.
- Action: Ethan to pull representative trace set and confirm sampling bias; Marissa to add dashboard panel showing kv-cache-hit-rate by host.

2026-03-31 (Tue)
- Follow-up: Ethan found that sampling window inadvertently excluded warmup spans for a subset of requests; after adjusting sampling filter we see consistent KV miss spikes aligned with autoscaler ramp events.
- Cost telemetry: Jorge reported a 12% token-cost increase for customers on model-x-8q in same window. Hypothesis: smaller batches + increased re-computation from cache misses increases per-token GPU time.
- Action: temporary mitigation -> throttle burst autoscaling (PR #412) landed in staging; testing queue length and latency regressions.

Observations & evidence:
- Tracing:
  - Span breakdown: attach_kv (new span introduced in runtime v2.3.1) accounts for 60% of the additional latency.
  - Correlation: high attach_kv durations co-occur with host-level memory pressure (swap_young > 60%).
  - Sampling gotcha: our existing sampling rule excluded spans with tag 'warmup=true' which filtered out several short-lived warm requests that exercise the cache warm path.
- Dashboards:
  - Current dashboards: latency-over-time (global) hides host-level variance. Need host-level panels and a per-model quantization profile breakdown.
  - Quick wins: add heatmap of kv-cache-hit-rate by host + a timeseries of attach_kv P95.
- Cost telemetry:
  - Billing-level spike maps to high small-batch usage from two enterprise customers using Dedicated pools with autoscale set to aggressive-burst.
  - Embedding batches not impacted; generation path primarily affected.

Investigations in progress:
- Reproduce: run load test with a mix of short-chat and long-chat to replicate KV miss pattern (Ethan). Steps in ticket JIRA-OBS-8741.
- Profiling: instrument the attach_kv span to include serialized cache key size and miss reason (Marissa).
- Autoscaler behavior: evaluate min-idle-policy changes vs. burst policy (Priya + SRE).

Dashboard tasks (short list):
- New panels to create:
  1) kv-cache-hit-rate (host, model, region) - target: P0 for next sprint. (owner: Marissa)
  2) attach_kv latency distribution by host - add jitter knobs. (owner: Ethan)
  3) cost-per-token trend split by model variant (fp16/8q/4q) - to show unit economics. (owner: Jorge)
- Alerts tweaks:
  - Add alert if kv-cache-hit-rate drops > 15% for 5m across > 20% hosts. Reduce noisy firing by excluding scheduled scale-down windows.

Cost telemetry actions:
- Short-term: rollback aggressive burst policy for two affected Dedicated pools; monitor cost metric for 24 hours. (owner: Priya)
- Mid-term: add cost-aware routing rule that prefers slightly larger batching windows for quantized models when cost delta > 7%. (owner: Product + Observability)

Action items (owners and status):
- Ethan Li: assemble trace corpus & repro harness; create runbook snippets (in progress). Linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412
- Marissa Clarke: implement kv-cache panels + add attach_kv labels (in progress).
- Jorge Alvarez: correlate billing logs with trace ids for affected customers and open chargeback notes (in_review).
- Priya Menon: coordinate temporary autoscaler throttle change and validate rollbacks (done in staging, monitoring in prod).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is the attach_kv span a symptom of a deeper memory fragmentation issue in the runtime? If yes, file an infra bug with heap/profile dump.
- Should we change default sampling rules to always capture first N warmup spans per host to avoid blind spots?
- How much unit-cost do we accept for the 8q variants if latencies improve for small chats? Need an SLO vs cost tradeoff doc.

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Lazy idea: have the autoscaler emit a short-lived 'scale_event' trace tag so we can slice traces by scale events without relying on timing windows. Low-effort: add tag at orchestrator level.
- Consider adding a small client-side jitter to avoid synchronized bursts hitting the same host pool (cheap mitigation).

Appendix: quick repro steps (for engineers)
1) Checkout telemetry branch with attach_kv instrumentation (branch: ops/kv-diagnostics).
2) Start local harness with 200 short-chat qps and 50 long-chat qps targeting model-x-8q.
3) Force autoscaler burst: hit orchestrator endpoint /scale?force=burst with region=us-west-2.
4) Collect traces from 03:00–03:10 window and run trace-diff script: tools/trace-diff --baseline=golden --window=600s.

Slack notes / refs:
- Slack thread: #obs-tracing "kv misses and cost uplift" (see thread ts:1623456789.000200)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/412
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-8741 (trace corpus + repro)

Closing thought: progress felt good this week — we have a plausible root cause (cache miss amplification during rapid scale events) and concrete mitigations (throttle burst + dashboarding). Next week focus: complete repro, verify cost deltas after throttle, and draft small SLO-vs-cost proposal for the product review.
